findings.title: In-place downsize uses the open tempfile path and ignores failure
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with the same path for input and output (tempfile.path, tempfile.path). ImageMagick convert cannot safely read and write the same file: it typically truncates the output before the input is fully read, producing an empty or corrupt image, or it replaces the inode while the open Tempfile fd still refers to the old file. Upload.create_for is then given that same tempfile and tempfile.size, so it can store the truncated/stale bytes rather than the resized image. The path also has no image extension (Rack/URL tempfiles are extensionless), so convert often cannot pick an output format, and the GIF branch never runs because optimize only treats a path matching /\.GIF$/i as animated. "80%" is also not a valid gifsicle --resize-fit size, so animated GIFs fail even when the extension is present. The return value is ignored and the loop does not reject the upload if the file is still larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb after five attempts, so a failed or insufficient shrink still proceeds to Upload.create_for.

findings.title: Second downsize definition silently replaces the width/height API
findings.body: Ruby keeps only the last def self.downsize. The new 3-argument form at line 149 replaces the width/height form at line 145, so that method is dead. Existing callers of OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) now bind max_height to opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] on an Integer and raises NoMethodError, and any resize geometry built from the numeric width is lost. Call sites that still pass width and height (thumbnail/downsize code outside this diff) will break at runtime.

findings.title: Client upload cap ignores per-type site settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments honored separate admin limits. It now always uses 10*1024 KB. Attachments larger than 10MB are rejected even when max_attachment_size_kb is higher, and images cannot exceed 10MB even when max_image_size_kb is higher (or 0, which this codebase treats as "do not enforce"). The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcode, so the file_too_large dialog reports 10240 KB regardless of the limit that actually rejected the upload.

findings.title: Multipart uploads are resized with no server-side size cap
findings.body: URL fetches were changed to a fixed 10.megabytes limit, but the new downsize loop on the multipart path has no upper bound. It runs ImageMagick (and ImageOptim inside convert_with) up to five times on any image larger than max_image_size_kb. The 10MB check exists only in client JS, which a direct POST or API upload can skip. A large or decompression-bomb image therefore reaches convert before Upload.create_for can reject it, tying up the deferred upload worker and memory.

findings.title: No test covers automatic downsize-on-upload
findings.body: The new shrink-before-create path has no test. A regression test would need an image over max_image_size_kb (including a GIF and an extensionless uploaded tempfile), assert the stored file is a valid image under the limit with updated filesize/dimensions, and assert that a failed or still-too-large downsize is rejected instead of saved. Without that, the in-place convert failure and the overridden downsize signature will not be caught.
